analysis.title: PJT Partners (PJT) Constructive outlook heading into 2027, with restructuring upside optionality, reiterate Buy
key_insights: GS reiterates Buy on PJT with the 12-month price target unchanged at $180. The stock was $153.58, implying 17.2% upside. GS calls the ~3% drop on the day a negative overreaction and a constructive entry point.

3Q26 adjusted EPS was $1.41 vs GSe $1.32 and Visible Alpha consensus $1.33. Normalizing for the lower tax rate, GS puts core EPS at $1.35. The 1% core beat vs the Street came entirely from 2% lower expenses, partly offset by 1% lower revenue.
3Q26 revenue was $385mn, 1% below consensus and down 14% YoY. Strategic advisory, private capital solutions and restructuring all declined. Primary fundraising revenue rose.

Management expects to enter 2027 with a meaningfully larger YoY pipeline of announced and pending transactions in Strategic Advisory. Cited supports are robust pre-announced pipelines, a benign near-term regulatory environment and corporate urgency to act. A lower deal conversion rate from elevated rates, costly debt financing and macro volatility partly offsets these.
Sponsor M&A recovery remains slow because of valuation disconnects and elevated borrowing costs. Higher-quality assets are less affected.

Restructuring demand stays high with a gradual mix shift toward in-court mandates. Management expects activity to persist or build, citing more debt outstanding with wider spreads, elevated rates, challenged business models, accelerating technological change and geopolitical uncertainty. A build is not in the company's budget, and GS says the upside optionality is better than it previously modeled.
PJT Park Hill faces a challenging primary fundraising environment. Management sees growing demand for alternative liquidity solutions because muted IPO markets limit portfolio monetization.

3Q26 pre-tax margin was ~50bps above the Street, entirely from a ~55bps lower non-comp ratio. Management kept the 2026 comp ratio of 66.5% and the 2026 non-comp dollar growth guide of close to 14% YoY despite ~5% lower 3Q26 non-comp. That implies 4Q26E non-comp ~3% above the Street.

The full-year 2026 effective tax rate guide was cut to 19.2% from 20.5%. An early read on the 2027E tax rate is ~25% because of lower tax deductions. GS raises its 2027E/28E tax rates by 330bps/280bps.

GS raises 2027E/28E revenue by 1%/2% and moves 2026E/27E/28E EPS by +1%/-4%/-2%, with the out-year cuts driven by the higher tax rate. 2026E/28E pre-tax margins change by -10bps/+10bps. The target multiple stays at 19.0x on 4Q27E-3Q28E EPS, so the target is unchanged.
GS estimates: net revenue of $1,858mn in 2026E, $2,117mn in 2027E and $2,271mn in 2028E. Diluted EPS is $7.48, $8.64 and $9.89. P/E is 20.5x, 17.8x and 15.5x.

market_movers.rationale: Constructive 2027 M&A pipeline and restructuring upside optionality. GS views the post-print share price drop as an overreaction. Target unchanged at 19.0x rolled-forward P/E.

earnings_insights: PJT 3Q26 adjusted EPS reported $1.41 (adjusted) vs GSe estimate $1.32 and Visible Alpha consensus estimate $1.33. GS core EPS, normalized for the lower tax rate, is $1.35.
3Q26 total revenue reported $385mn, 1% below consensus estimate and down 14% YoY.
3Q26 margins were ~50bps above the Street estimate, entirely from a ~55bps lower non-comp ratio. 3Q26 non-comp dollars were ~5% lower YoY.

Guidance reiterated: 2026 comp ratio 66.5% (management best estimate), 2026 non-comp dollar growth close to 14% YoY. Full-year 2026 effective tax rate guide lowered to 19.2% from 20.5%, with an early read of ~25% for 2027.
GS implies 4Q26E non-comp expense growth of ~19% YoY and ~14% QoQ, ~3% above the Street estimate, assuming ~13.5% YoY growth in 2026E non-comp dollars.

trade_ideas.description: Long PJT equity, Buy rating, 12-month price target $180 vs $153.58 price
trade_ideas.rationale: Constructive 2027 M&A trajectory and restructuring upside optionality, with the post-earnings drop seen as an overreaction.
trade_ideas.risk: Weaker M&A backlogs, longer time to completion pushing out M&A and restructuring revenue, slower scaling, inability to drive margin catch-up, longer-term share losses.
